g.title: storyline
g.text: Storyline: Does Visual Contrastive Decoding still help on degraded images?
LLaVA-1.5-7B on POPE · AUROC on the 400 test images, mean of 3 splits · green = helps, orange = does not help

g.title: q
g.text: VCD subtracts the output for a diffusion-noised copy of the image.
It assumes the image is clean. What if it is already blurred or noisy?
Hypothesis: the two passes converge, so VCD's gain shrinks with degradation.

g.title: setup
g.text: 500 COCO images, 3 POPE splits (random / popular / adversarial)
Gaussian blur σ 5 / 7 / 10 / 16 and noise std 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 / 1.0
Levels calibrated in a pilot run (a first, weaker ladder had no effect)

g.title: repro
g.text: Within 0.5 F1 of the paper with T = 999
Already on clean images most of the gain is a higher yes-rate

g.title: diag
g.text: … but it is a threshold shift, not better grounding
Baseline moved to VCD's yes-rate matches or beats VCD's F1
AUROC unchanged (−0.0024) once forced answers are ranked consistently
The passes do converge: JS divergence halves

g.title: proto
g.text: 100 dev images for all choices · 400 test images for results
AUROC + matched-threshold baseline + paired bootstrap CIs

g.title: dola
g.text: JS layer choice breaks the output

g.title: dae
g.text: VCD on restored image (B1): best F1

g.title: negsum
g.text: Everything that subtracts or re-weights the final layer
stays within about ±0.003 mean AUROC of the baseline:
it cannot add evidence the degraded image has lost

g.title: final
g.text: 6 views incl. the restored image, layer 20
Dev picks α = 0: VCD's contrast is
+0.032 mean AUROC · better in 26/27, never worse
F1 up to +6.7 over an equally tuned baseline
Views + layer handle blur, the DAE handles noise

g.title: concl
g.text: On degraded images VCD recalibrates rather than grounds.
Report AUROC and a matched-threshold baseline, not F1 alone.
Adding evidence (views, a middle layer, restoration) is what helps.
